turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Why do you hesitate, child? Do you not wish to amuse me?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm very sorry, ma'am, but I don't think I'm suited to play with you. You see, I'm only a poor boy from the village.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Poverty is no barrier to pleasure, I assure you. Call Estella.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: But, ma'am, I'm afraid I'm not really fit for play. I'm not used to such grand things.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Fit for play? You are a boy, are you not? Boys are always fit for play.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, ma'am, but I don't think it's suitable for me to play with you, considering...

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Considering what, child? Speak quickly, I am impatient.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Considering my sister's wishes, ma'am, and our family's circumstances.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Your sister's wishes? Ha! I'll have you know, child, I am not to be trifled with.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: No, ma'am, I'm sure you're not, and I'm grateful for your kindness.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Kindness? Bah! I am a just and fair mistress. Call Estella.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: But, ma'am, I'm not sure I want to play with Estella either. She seems... distant.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Distant? Ah, yes. Estella is a child of my heart. But she will play with you, I am sure.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm not sure I'm worthy of her company, ma'am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Worthy? Ha! You are here, are you not? And that is all that matters.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, ma'am, but I don't want to be a bother.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: A bother? I am a woman who has been jilted at the altar. You are but a child.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm sorry for your pain, ma'am, and I'll try to be more cheerful.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Cheerful? Ha! You will play with Estella, and you will be grateful for my hospitality.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, ma'am, I'll try my best.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.
